manifest.name: dsh-cost-pill
manifest.description: DeepSeek account balance and per-session cost pill for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): official peak/off-peak token pricing, web search/fetch per-request fees, subagent sessions included, per-model breakdown, no credentials stored.

bundle.text:
# dsh 组合包补丁:把本插件的宿主半边挂进某个 profile。
# 客户端半边是清单里 `dsh.client` 声明的浏览器行,由模块清单扫描后装载,
# 因此这里只插入宿主那一行。
- insert:
    - id: cost-stats
      name: 'dsh-cost-pill'

readme.text: **Account balance and cost statistics** pill for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It adds a pill at the right-hand end of the official stats row below the session composer, combining three readings: the billing period (peak / off-peak, colour-coded), the account balance, and the current session cost. Clicking the pill expands a per-session breakdown — cache-hit input, cache-miss input and output amounts, cost per model, the successful web search / web fetch call counts and their per-request fee (billed from 2026-11-01), and the token and web-call cost of the subagent sessions this session spawned (at any depth). The cost side needs no credentials; the balance side needs a DeepSeek API key.
> Community plugin. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or shipped by DeepSeek.

- **Rightmost pill in the stats row**: registers into `conversation.composer.dock` with `order: 2`, after both official stats pills (`activity` = 0, `usage` = 1). The period reads `Peak` or `Off-peak`, and a red / green dot distinguishes them.
- **Popup breakdown**: billing period, account balance, current session cost, the cost split by bucket — cache-hit input, cache-miss input (cache writes included), output — a per-model breakdown whenever the host can fold one, and the session's successful web search / web fetch call counts and fee when it made such calls. Subagent spend is not a separate line: it is folded into every amount above; when subagents exist, the session-cost label reads "(incl. subagents)" and a small note says how many sessions are included.
- **Subagent spend included**: every descendant subagent session (identified by the `origin: subagent` header lineage, including subagents of subagents) has its token usage and web call fees folded into the existing fields — total, the three token buckets, the web rows and the per-model rows. A user fork is an independent conversation and never counts. Running subagents are read from memory; closed ones are read from their per

- DeepSeek Harness (dsh) `>= 0.2.1-rc.2`.
- A DeepSeek **API key** if you want the balance. It is resolved through dsh's credentials seam; the plugin falls back to the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` environment variable **only when the credentials service itself is unavailable** — if credentials exists but holds no such key, the environment variable is not consulted. When no key resolves (for example an install signed in with a DeepSeek *account*), the pill keeps showing the billing period and the session cost, and only the balance is absent.

From the plugin market (search `dsh-cost`), or from a terminal:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-cost-pill
```

You can also install from the GitHub source: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Arun1016/dsh-cost`.

> Note: the bare npm name `dsh-cost` belongs to an unrelated project; this plugin is published under the `@arun_1016/` scope, so the two cannot be confused.

```yaml
- id: cost-stats
  name: dsh-cost
  config:
    holidays: ['2026-01-01']   # statutory holidays bill off-peak all day

`holidays` is the only Config field. It defaults to the built-in 2026 PRC statutory-holiday table (State Council notice 国办发明电〔2025〕7号), as Beijing-local `YYYY-MM-DD` dates. A new year is a Config edit, not a code change.

Model prices are CNY per million tokens, and every figure below is a **peak** rate — off-peak is exactly half, per the official rule. Search and Fetch are billed per request instead, listed at the end of the table.

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Flash (from 2026-09-10 12:00 Beijing) | peak `2 / 0.04 / 8` = uncached input / cache-hit input / output |
| Flash (before the price cut) | `3.0 / 0.1 / 9.0`, same three buckets |
| Pro (`deepseek-v4-pro`, before 2026-09-14 12:00 Beijing) | `9.0 / 0.3 / 27.0`, same three buckets |
| Peak window | workdays `09:00–12:00` and `14:00–18:00` |
| Off-peak | everything else; weekends and statutory holidays all day, including a weekend that holiday adjustment turns into a workday |
| Clock used | the local clock of the machine running dsh — the official windows are Beijing time, so the reading is only exact on a Beijing-time host |
| pro→flash routing | billed as Flash from 2026-09-14 12:00 Beijing |
| `inputTokens` | uncached input; cache writes bill at the uncached rate |
| reasoning | subset of output, not billed separately |
| Search / Fetch calls | ¥5 per 1,000 successful requests (¥0.005 each), independent of the peak / off-peak window |
| Web billing start | 2026-11-01 00:00 Beijing; earlier successful calls cost nothing and display as "Free" |
| Successful call | Search returned a non-empty `results` array; Fetch returned page content; failures, empty sea

The Search / Fetch price and billing start come from the official [price page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing) and the [web search & fetch guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/search) (announced 2026-10-17).

- No telemetry, no analytics, no third-party endpoints.
- The only outbound request is `https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`, authenticated with your key; it times out after 15 s.
- The browser half only reads the host route `/api/dsh-balance` — once per session step, plus a 60 s poll. It never contacts a third-party endpoint itself.
- This plugin never writes the key to disk, and balances are cached in memory only.

- While the session is attached the host folds usage per request, so a span across the price cut, the routing change or a peak boundary keeps its own rate table. A **detached** session is priced by the host as one aggregate at the current Flash rates and carries **no** estimate marker; the browser half's own fallback estimate uses the same current rates and is marked `(估)` in Chinese / `(est)` in English.
- Web search / fetch fees are inferred from the session log's `web_search` / `web_fetch` tool calls: the host does not load a detached session's log and keeps no per-query results, so **detached sessions** and the **local fallback estimate** omit this fee; a log trimmed by compaction undercounts too.
- A multi-query `web_search` whose queries partly return nothing cannot be split after the results are merged, so every distinct query is billed (an overcount); a failed call bills nothing, but sibling requests that had already succeeded in the same batch cannot be counted (an undercount).
- A web fee is priced by when the tool result landed, so a request straddling 2026-11-01 00:00 Beijing can land on either side of the billing start by seconds.
- Subagent spend depends on dsh's sess

Source lives in `src/` (host half `index.ts`, client half `client/`). It is built with the official dsh monorepo toolchain: `tsconfig.*.json` and `tsdown.config.ts` reference the monorepo through relative paths (`../../../tsconfig.base.json`, `../../client/tsdown.client.ts`), so building requires placing this package back into that tree — the repository cannot be built standalone.
The published package carries `lib/` and `cordis.patch.yml`, plus `package.json`, both READMEs and `LICENSE` (npm always includes those).
